lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Saturday, 9 a.m. Her little brother's birthday party starts at 4.
**Mum:** Twenty kids at the void deck at four o'clock! Dad, you're making the **cake**.
**Dad:** A cake? **Piece of cake.**
**Ah Boy:** I'm turning **eight**, so I want **⅛** of the cake. Eight is the **biggest** number!
**Kavya:** Ah Boy, **¼** is bigger than **⅛**.
**Ah Boy:** Eight is bigger than four. I've done maths.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the little line on Mum's measuring jug.
**Vinny:** Vinny. The **fraction bar**. I work the door. **Tops** upstairs. **Bottoms** downstairs.
**Vinny:** Upstairs, the **numerator**: the pieces you've got. Downstairs, the **denominator**: how many equal pieces make **one whole**.
**Vinny:** Cut a cake into **8** and the pieces are smaller than cutting it into **4**. So **⅛ < ¼**.
**Ah Boy:** Then I want **one-oneth**!
**Vinny:** That's the **whole cake**, kid.
**Vinny:** House rules: **same-size pieces**. And nobody adds the bottoms. **Not on my bar.**
**Narrator:** Piece of Cake. Episode 4: Ah Boy Turns Eight.
**Narrator:** 10 a.m. The void deck. Priya has come to help. Competitively.
**Priya:** Priya. Best friend. **42** of my **56** balloons done: **42/56**!
**Vinny:** Too crowded upstairs. **Simplest form**: divide top **and** bottom by the **HCF**.
**Vinny:** **Equivalent fractions**: same number, new name. Multiply or divide top and bottom by the **same** number.
**Priya:** Now **49** of **56**: **⅞**. And you?
**Kavya:** **8** of my **9** goodie bags: **8/9**. We're both **one piece short**.
**Kavya:** But **ninths** are smaller pieces. My gap is smaller, so I'm **closer to one**.
**Vinny:** Check with a **common denominator**, **72**: ⅞ = **63/72**, 8/9 = **64/72**. **8/9 wins**.
**Priya:** I demand a recount.
**Narrator:** 11 a.m. Number-line hopscotch, from **−1** to **1**.
**Ah Boy:** I'm on **−¾**! It beats **−⅔**, because ¾ beats ⅔!
**Mira:** Mira. The **mirror at zero**. I show the right side on the left. **Backwards**.
**Mira:** So the order **flips**. −¾ is further **left**: **−¾ < −⅔**.
**Kavya:** Use tenths: −6, −5, −4. So **−⅗ < −½ < −⅖ < 0 < ¼**.
**Ah Boy:** Mirror, mirror, at zero. Who's the **smallest** of them all?
**Mira:** It's **negative three fifths**, darling.
**Priya:** So **−½ ≥ −⅖**, true or false?
**Kavya:** **False.** −½ is further **left**.
**Narrator:** 12 p.m. The kitchen. Dad has never baked a cake.
**Dad:** **⅔** of a cup of sugar, plus **⅗**. Add the tops, add the bottoms: **5/8**. Piece of cake.
**Vinny:** **Not on my bar!**
**Kavya:** Dad, **5/8** is less than the **⅔** on its own.
**Vinny:** The bottom is the **size** of the piece. Make them the **same size**: the LCM, **15**.
**Kavya:** **10/15 + 9/15 = 19/15**. Add the tops, keep the bottom.
**Topsy:** Topsy! **Improper fraction**. My top's bigger than my bottom. I'm **top-heavy**! Help!
**Kavya:** 19 ÷ 15 = 1 remainder 4: **1 4/15** cups. A **mixed number**.
**Topsy:** One **whole** to sit on. Much better.
**Ah Boy:** And **2 ⅗** back to top-heavy?
**Kavya:** **MAD**: **M**ultiply 2 × 5, **A**dd 3, **D**enominator stays: **13/5**.
**Kavya:** **Estimate**: just over 3, minus nearly 2. It must be between **1** and **2**.
**Vinny:** Backwards! **¼** is smaller than **⅔**. **Borrow a whole.**
**Ah Boy:** Or **count up**! **⅓** to get to 2, **1** to get to 3, **¼** more. **1 7/12**!
**Dad:** Good news: the cake is in the oven. Bad news: it has **5/8** of a cup of sugar in it.
**Narrator:** 2 p.m. The cake survived. It is a rectangle, and it has **opinions**.
**Victoria:** Victoria. **Sponge cake**. Whatever you do, darling, cut me into **equal pieces**.
**Mum:** Chocolate on **¾** of the width. Sprinkles on **⅔** of the length.
**Ah Boy:** I want the bits with **both**. What fraction is that?
**Vinny:** **4** columns, **3** rows: **12** equal pieces. Both toppings: **6**.
**Kavya:** So **¾ × ⅔ = 6/12 = ½**. Multiply the tops, multiply the bottoms.
**Victoria:** Half of me has chocolate **and** sprinkles. I've never felt so **seen**.
**Ah Boy:** **Times** makes things **bigger**. So **¾** of the **20** sweets is **more** than 20!
**Mum:** '**Of**' means **times**: 20 × ¾ = **15**. A **proper fraction** makes it **smaller**.
**Ah Boy:** I would like a **refund** on maths.
**Priya:** Speed round! **⅚ × 9/10**!
**Vinny:** **Cancel first.** Any top with any bottom: 5 with 10, 9 with 6. That leaves **¾**.
**Dad:** Picnic mat: **2 ½** m by **3 ⅓** m. 2 × 3 = 6, ½ × ⅓ = ⅙. **6 ⅙**! Piece of cake.
**Vinny:** **Not on my bar!**
**Kavya:** **Improper first**: 5/2 × 10/3 = 50/6 = **8 ⅓** m².
**Mum:** Integer times mixed: **3** tables of **2 ¾** m. 3 × 2 + 3 × ¾ = 6 + 2 ¼ = **8 ¼** m.
**Narrator:** 3 p.m. Three pizzas arrive. Mum cuts each one into **quarters**.
**Ah Boy:** **3 ÷ ¼**. Dividing makes things **smaller**, so less than 3 slices.
**Kavya:** Division asks **how many fit**. **4** quarters in each pizza, so **3 ÷ ¼ = 12**.
**Ah Boy:** Twelve slices out of three pizzas? That's **witchcraft**.
**Flip:** Not witchcraft! **Gymnastics**! I'm Flip! The **reciprocal**!
**Flip:** Times by your reciprocal and you get **1**. ⅖ flips to **5/2**. **7** to **1/7**. **1 ¾** = 7/4, so **4/7**. Zero? **No** reciprocal.
**Flip:** To **divide** by a fraction, multiply by its **reciprocal**. **Keep, Change, Flip!**
**Priya:** **⅔ ÷ ⅘**. Flip them **both**!
**Flip:** No! Only the **second** one flips: the **divisor**. **⅔ × 5/4 = 10/12 = ⅚**.
**Mum:** Lime juice: **2 ¼** litres. Cups of **⅜** of a litre. How many cups?
**Kavya:** **Improper first**: 2 ¼ = 9/4. Then **9/4 × 8/3**.
**Flip:** Cancel 9 with 3, and 8 with 4: 3 × 2 = **6 cups**!
**Mum:** And the last **¾** of a pizza, for **6** kids: ¾ ÷ 6 = ¾ × ⅙ = **⅛** each.
**Ah Boy:** I get an **eighth**! The **biggest** number! Finally!
**Narrator:** 4 p.m. The party starts. Eighteen kids. Two hundred and forty sweets.
**Mum:** **⅗** of the sweets are chocolate. How many?
**Kavya:** Divide by the **bottom**, times the **top**: 240 ÷ 5 = **48**, 48 × 3 = **144**.
**Ah Boy:** Grandma gave me money. I spent **⅜** on a robot. **$15** left. How much did she give me?
**Kavya:** Bar model: **8** boxes. Robot: **3**. So **5** boxes = **$15**.
**Kavya:** **Find one part first**: 1 box = **$3**. 8 boxes = **$24**.
**Vinny:** Or in one step: **15 ÷ ⅝ = 15 × 8/5 = 24**.
**Ah Boy:** So the robot cost **$9**. Grandma does not need to know.
**Mr Tan:** Good afternoon! Mr Tan, eighth floor. Party games: **45 minutes** of your **2 hours**.
**Ah Boy:** So the games are **45/2** of the party!
**Kavya:** **Same units first!** 2 hours = **120** minutes. **45/120 = ⅜**.
**Mum:** **18** kids this year, **12** last year: **18/12 = 1 ½** times as many. More than **1**!
**Dad:** One and a half times the **noise**.
**Priya:** I spent **⅓** of my money on Ah Boy's present, then **¼** of the **remainder** on bubble tea. **$18** left.
**Kavya:** **Of the remainder**: ¼ of the ⅔ left is **⅙**. Spent: ⅓ + ⅙ = **½**.
**Kavya:** So **½** is **$18**. You started with **$36**.
**Ah Boy:** So my present cost **$12**?
**Priya:** It's the **thought** that counts.
**Narrator:** 5 p.m. Pass the parcel. Under every layer, a calculation. Mr Tan wrapped it himself.
**Mr Tan:** Layer one! **7/9 × 13 + 7/9 × 5**. Ten seconds!
**Mr Tan:** Layer two! **½ + ⅓ × ¾**.
**Dad:** Left to right: ⅚ × ¾ = **⅝**. Piece of cake.
**Vinny:** **Not on my bar.**
**Mr Tan:** **Order of operations**: multiply **before** you add. ⅓ × ¾ = ¼, then ½ + ¼ = **¾**. Your ⅝ needs **brackets**.
**Mr Tan:** Layer three: **commutative** law! **3/7 × 15 × 7/3**. Swap the order: 3/7 × 7/3 = **1**, so **15**.
**Kavya:** And **(⅔)² = 4/9**: square the top **and** the bottom.
**Mr Tan:** Always **estimate**: 2 ⅞ × 3 9/10 ≈ 3 × 4 = **12**. Both rounded **up**, so a bit **less**.
**Mr Tan:** 'Fraction' comes from the Latin **frangere**: to **break**. So fractions are great at breaking the ice.
**Ah Boy:** Is there a **prize** in the middle?
**Mr Tan:** The last layer! Think of any number, **x**. Not zero. Work out **x/3 × 6/x**.
**Ah Boy:** I picked **a million**! It's still **2**?!
**Mister X:** Mister X. **The unknown**. I can be **any** number. Except zero. I don't do zero.
**Mister X:** An **x** on top, an **x** on the bottom: we **cancel**. **6x/3x = 2**. Every time.
**Mr Tan:** Harder! **2x/3 × 9/(4x)**. **Cancel first.**
**Kavya:** x with x, 2 with 4, 9 with 3. That leaves **3/2**, or **1 ½**.
**Mr Tan:** Dividing: **keep, change, flip**, then cancel. **4x/9 ÷ 2x/3 = 4x/9 × 3/(2x) = ⅔**.
**Ah Boy:** So **(x + 5)/(x + 7)** is **5/7**! Cancel the x's!
**Mister X:** No. That **+ 5** is stuck to me. Only **factors** cancel: things that **multiply** the whole top and the whole bottom.
**Mr Tan:** That's why Mister X is my favourite guest. He always **cancels**.

chapters.title: The party saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the cake, the party would like to save you some marks.
**Dad:** One. **Never, ever add the bottoms.** Ask my cake.
**Kavya:** Two. **Borrow a whole**: 3 ¼ − 1 ⅔ is **1 7/12**, not 2 5/12.
**Flip:** Three. Only the **second** fraction flips. The first one stays on its feet.
**Priya:** Four. '**Of the remainder**' means a fraction of what's **left**. I learnt that with my own money.
**Ah Boy:** Five. **Same units first**: 45 minutes of 2 hours is **45/120**.
**Mr Tan:** Six. Only cancel **factors**. **(x + 6)/(x + 3)** is **not** 2.
**Narrator:** Piece of Cake will return.
**Narrator:** 6 p.m. The cake.
**Mum:** Birthday boy! Which piece? A **quarter**? An **eighth**?
**Ah Boy:** I've learnt my lesson. **Smaller** bottom, **bigger** piece. So I want...
**Ah Boy:** ...**one-oneth**.
**Mum:** ...It's your birthday.
**Victoria:** Finally. Someone who sees me as a **whole**.
**Vinny:** Simplest form. ...Beautiful.
